records.name: IAMM Science Education Group
records.summary: Uses science education and open discussion to help Black and Brown students and their communities get into STEAM fields (science, technology, engineering, arts, and math). It runs community screenings and talks and has a scholarship fund.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a community screening, sign up to volunteer or mentor through the contact form, or apply for the scholarship fund.

schedule.text: The Philly Salon screenings are one-time events, not a regular timetable, and the site lists no fixed days or times.

cost.text: Ticket price not shown; donations suggested from $25

first_step.how: Email iammscience@gmail.com or use the contact form on iammscience.com to ask about volunteering, mentoring, or the next screening.
first_step.basis: Screenings are open to anyone who buys a ticket, and the site has a public way to ask about volunteering and mentoring, but it does not describe a newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Philly Salon screening is a set of documentary films shown at Scribe Video on Lancaster Avenue, and the series pairs the films with community dialogue. Tickets are sold online through a link on the site, and the site shows no ticket price.
first_visit_tips: Look for the next Philly Salon date on the site, since screenings are not on a fixed schedule.
Get your ticket through the online link on the site.
The site has no accessibility details, so email ahead with any access questions.

records.notes: The site is one page with sections and no separate volunteer, mentoring, FAQ or accessibility pages. A guessed contact page returned not found. The 25 dollar donation figure comes from tier 1 and was not seen on the site this time.

records.name: IBOA International Basketball Officials Academy
records.summary: A Philadelphia program that teaches FIBA 3x3 basketball to young people through clinics, camps and tournaments, including sessions at city recreation centers. It also trains and mentors basketball referees.
records.what_you_do: Kids and teens can take part in 3x3 clinics, camps and tournaments when they run. Adults can volunteer for check-in, court setup, scoring, youth support or media through the volunteer form on the site.

schedule.text: Youth 3x3 clinics, camps and tournaments run when they are announced. The site does not publish fixed days or times.

cost.text: No clinic or camp prices are published on the site. The site asks for donations.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list on the Contact page for notices about youth clinics and tournaments, or send the volunteer form from the Become a Volunteer page.
first_step.basis: Youth programs are open to kids and teens, and the site has a mailing list and a volunteer form, but the steps to sign up for a clinic are not published.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers can help for a few hours or a full day. Roles include check-in, court setup, scoring, youth support and media, and the site says no experience is needed. Past tournaments were held at Pelbano Recreation Center, but the site does not say when clinics meet.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether volunteers who work with young people need background clearances, since the site does not say.
Email info@iboa3x3.com or call 267-268-9022 to ask about the next clinic or camp.
The academy office is at 2650 Welsh Road, and the site gives no bus, train or parking details.

records.notes: The events page lists a free June 20, 2026 tournament at Pelbano Recreation Center with 16U and 18U divisions and a 13U Rising Stars challenge. The recap page says 12U for Rising Stars, so that age is unclear. A FIBA 3x3 Officiating Basics webinar on October 14, 2026 costs 40 dollars and is limited to 25 people. It is a one-time event, so it is noted here and in last_sign_of_life, not in the schedule. IBOA Officials (iboaofficials.org) is the referee branch of this same nonprofit, so it is covered by this record and is not a separate lead. The site does not say which recreation centers host clinics.

records.name: IGDA Philly
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the International Game Developers Association. It holds free monthly meetings where local game makers give talks, with networking time first. Meetings are in person at Drexel or online.
records.what_you_do: Attend a free monthly meeting with 30 minutes of networking, then talks by local developers. Join the chapter's Discord to hear about upcoming meetings.

schedule.text: Monthly evening meetings, with about 30 minutes of networking before the talks. Meetings are in person at the URBN Center at Drexel University or online by Zoom webinar.

first_step.how: RSVP for an in-person meeting through the chapter's Discord event link, or use the registration link on the meeting listing to join online by Zoom.
first_step.basis: Meetings are free and open to the public with a posted way to register, but the chapter does not describe a newcomer or beginner program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings run in the evening. The May 2026 meeting ran from 7 to 9 pm, with 30 minutes of networking before talks that began at 7:30. The May session was a panel on interactive narrative design, and it took questions from the audience.
first_visit_tips: Arrive by 7 pm to catch the networking time before the talks.
Enter the URBN Center at 3501 Market Street, Room 125, at Drexel University.
Email IGDAPhilly@gmail.com if you are unsure how to register.

records.notes: The chapter events page (igda.org/events) lists only events in other countries right now, under a 2019 header, so no upcoming Philadelphia meeting is confirmed. Chapter news items mention a January assembly and a February talk with no year, so they were not used. The chapter page gives no meeting times or newcomer information. Online registration uses a short link on the event listing, which is not recorded here.

records.name: IHM Center for Literacy
records.summary: An adult literacy center that supports immigrants' inclusion in American society. It teaches English and basic computer use, and it takes volunteer tutors and new students through a phone line and online forms.
records.what_you_do: Students build English, reading and computer skills, and can also get citizenship classes and help with job, school and immigration forms. Volunteers tutor adult learners. Both paths start with a form or a phone call.

schedule.text: Classes meet Monday to Thursday in two morning sessions (9 to 10:30 am and 10:45 am to 12:15 pm) and one evening session (6:45 to 8:15 pm).

cost.text: Tuition and fees are not stated on the site. Ask when you call.

first_step.how: Call 215-338-3120 or fill out the Student Interest Form on the website. New students then take a placement test and book an in-person appointment.
first_step.basis: The about page says learners at every stage of English are welcome, and the classes page lays out the steps: an interest form or a call, a placement test, then an in-person appointment.
first_step.what_to_expect: New students take a placement test that sets a level from Basic up to Intermediate. Classes are small, with 5 to 20 students, and meet on weekday mornings or evenings. The site does not say what the placement test covers, how long it takes, or what classes cost.
first_visit_tips: Call during office hours: Monday to Thursday, 8:30 am to 1 pm, or 6:15 to 8 pm. The office is closed Friday to Sunday.
Ask about fees and the placement test on the phone, since the website does not state them.
The site gives no bus, train or parking details, so ask about getting there when you call.

records.notes: The about page gives 4521 L Street for the 2022 consolidation, but the classes page and an NLD directory listing both give 4251 L Street, so 4251 is used. The 4521 figure is probably a typo but is not confirmed. The email from tier 1 is hidden behind email protection on the site and was not re-read. The contact page has only a form. The classes page says classes began in September 2025 and gives no current term dates.

records.name: Immaculate Heart of Mary Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on East Cathedral Road with three Sunday Masses and weekday morning Mass.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or call the parish office to ask about classes. Children in grades 1 to 7 can join the religious education program (PREP) on Tuesday evenings during the school year. New parishioners can ask the pastor for a home visit.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 7:30, 9:30 and 11:30 am. Saturday vigil Mass at 5:15 pm and Saturday Mass at 8 am. Weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 8:30 am in the Chapel, or in the church on Wednesdays during the school year. Saturday confession 4 to 5 pm.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass at 7:30, 9:30 or 11:30 am, or call the parish office at 215-483-1000 to ask about classes or set up a visit with the pastor.
first_step.basis: The welcome page greets new members and invites them to contact the pastor for a home visit, and Mass is open to anyone at the posted times.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is open to anyone at the posted times. The church was built in 1965 and seats about 1,000 people. The site does not say how long Mass lasts or what visitors do, so the parish office is the best place to ask.
first_visit_tips: Weekday Mass is in the Chapel at 8:30 am, except on Wednesdays during the school year, when it is in the church.
The rectory is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm. Call first if you want to meet the pastor.
For religious education in grades 1 to 7, new students need a baptismal certificate to register.

records.notes: The religious education page has a 2026 to 2027 registration heading, but the only start date it gives is for 2024 and the registration deadline has no year, so no registration dates are recorded. Parking and entrances are not on the site. The religious education office has its own phone number on its page. The bulletin ad lists two different email addresses, so confirm which one to use.

records.name: Immanuel Lutheran Church
records.summary: A Lutheran congregation in the Somerton area of Northeast Philadelphia that worships on Sundays in person and on Zoom. It also lists a German-language service and a Trunk or Treat.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship in person or on Zoom, come to a listed event, or call the office to arrange a visit. The church also lists groups such as a German circle and a women's group, and the site does not say how to join them.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:15 am, in person and on Zoom. German-language services are listed for some Sundays, and the church lists other events as they come up.

cost.text: No fees are listed on the site. Online giving is offered.

access.notes: Ramps, an elevator and an accessible restroom, per the home page.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:15 am, in person or on Zoom. To ask questions or arrange a visit, call 215-464-1540 or email office@immanuelphilly.org.
first_step.basis: The site invites visitors to Sunday worship in person or on Zoom, and it gives an office phone and email for questions or a visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: Services are held in person and on Zoom at the same time. The site does not say how long worship lasts, what to wear, or whether children have a separate program during the service. The office can answer those questions before you come.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the Sunday time with the office, since two church pages list different times.
The church has ramps, an elevator and an accessible restroom.
The site does not give a Zoom link, so ask the office for one if you plan to join online.

records.notes: The home page lists events on October 10, 13, 18 and 31 with no year written, so the status stays probably active and no last sign of life is recorded. The 10:15 am time comes from the home page. An older worship page lists 9:30 am and 11:00 am German services, which conflicts with the home page. The Kids Connection page says that program is on hiatus, so no children's program is listed. The older worship page also describes a casual preaching style and says newcomers can try the choirs, but that page is undated and was not used for the record.

records.name: Independence Squares
records.summary: A square dance club for LGBTQ+ dancers in Philadelphia. Members dance modern Western square dance, and you change partners with each tip, so you can come without a partner.
records.what_you_do: Take a beginner class in the fall, come to a summer open house, or join the Tuesday evening classes and dances. Saturday dances run at several levels, so check the dance schedule before you go.

schedule.text: Beginner classes meet Tuesdays, 7 to 9:30 pm, from fall into spring. Saturday dances run through the year on set dates, some in the afternoon and some in the evening. The dance schedule page lists them.

locations.label: Lutheran Church of the Holy Communion (most dances)

cost.text: Beginner classes cost $5 per class for new Mainstream dancers and members, and $7 for non-members. Most Saturday dances cost $10 per session, or $15 for a two-session event. Open houses are usually $5. Club dues of $45 cover June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027, and first-time Mainstream dancers do not owe dues. Reduced admission is available by confidential application.

first_step.how: Come to a Tuesday beginner (Mainstream) class at 2111 Sansom St at 7 pm. No partner is needed. You join a set when the music starts and change partners as you go. Pay $5 at the class.
first_step.basis: Beginner classes run each fall for people new to square dancing, first-time Mainstream dancers do not owe dues, and no partner is needed. The page does not say whether the Saturday dances suit beginners.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Tuesday class runs 7 to 9:30 pm, led by callers, and it alternates between Week A and Week B. You do not need a partner. Wear what you like, such as jeans and a t-shirt. First-time Mainstream dancers do not owe club dues, but each class is $5.
first_visit_tips: Arrive a few minutes early and use the back entrance at 2111 Sansom St.
A nearby garage offers discounted parking. Ask at check-in for the QR code.
Bring a snack to share, as the club suggests.
Wear comfortable clothes, such as jeans and a t-shirt.

records.notes: The fall beginner start date (September 22) is written without a year, so no year is recorded for it. The class schedule image on the classes page could not be read, so the weekly pattern is only given as Week A and Week B. The dance schedule lists a December 5, 2026 Glitter Ball at Merion Friends Meetinghouse with a level listing that may be a typo, so it is not used. The site does not say whether Saturday dances suit beginners. The phrase about partners changing every 15 minutes in tier 1 is not on the page, so the summary now says partners change with each tip.
